results.reason: Asks whether to build a requested feature at all, which is exactly the go/no-go challenge this skill owns.
Explicit request to reduce complexity and surface area of an over-engineered component while keeping behavior.
Directly asks for acceptance criteria before implementation begins.
Request to review a specific PR for defects, including a migration in the change.
Intermittent production failures after a deploy with an explicit ask to find the actual cause.
Splitting a large service into modules without changing behavior is the core refactor scenario.
Asks how to test a flow with almost no tests and limited time, i.e. prioritizing what to test.
Audit of uploads and admin endpoints before internet exposure is squarely a security review.
Concrete slow page and slow API endpoint with a request to make them faster via measurement.
Large-table column rename requiring zero downtime is the canonical migration-safety case.
Designing partner-facing endpoints, error shapes, pagination, and versioning is a contract design task.
The complaint names the exact generic AI page patterns this skill removes.
Rewriting an error message to tell the user what happened and what to do next is explicitly covered.
Splitting a mixed branch into reviewable commits and writing the PR description is the skill's purpose.
WCAG failure on a form with keyboard, label, and focus problems is a direct a11y audit request.
Variant sprawl and raw hex values are the exact inconsistency this skill addresses via tokens and migration.
Janky, slow modal motion plus gratuitous hover scale is precisely the motion decision this skill owns.
Asks for logs, metrics, traces, and alerts for a new service before on-call.
Requests a go/no-go decision with blockers for a risky Friday deploy.
Build-vs-buy on date-fns versus moment plus auditing the dependency tree.
Screenshot given as the specification with a demand to replicate the UI exactly into HTML/CSS.
A trivial broken-button CSS fix; debug-root-cause uses the word broken but a one-line style fix is not root-cause diagnosis.
A query scanning two million rows on every request is a clear measurement-driven performance fix.
Adding tests is covered, and a blanket demand for twenty tests is exactly the coverage-theater behavior this skill pushes back on.
A straightforward implementation request for a validation function; no listed skill owns writing it.
Adding structured logging and a dashboard to a service is instrumenting for production debuggability.
Renaming one local variable is mechanical, not a behavior-preserving restructuring effort.
Raising the timeout papers over the symptom; this skill explicitly prevents symptom patches, so it owns correcting the approach.
A GDPR consent banner is legal/compliance UI work; no listed skill covers consent or privacy requirements.
Cloud cost reduction is an infrastructure spend problem, not runtime performance optimization.
Writing an ad-hoc SQL report query is ordinary data querying, not schema or data migration.
Calling a third-party API to create a charge is integration usage, not API design or contract work.
Translation of existing text into another language is not prose crafting or rewriting.
Summarizing a PDF into bullets is extraction and condensation, not writing or rewriting prose.
Resolving a merge conflict in a manifest file is mechanical git work, not PR shaping or refactoring.
Moving and resizing a logo is a single visual tweak with no accessibility, system, or motion concern asked for.
Brand palette and logo direction is identity design, not component tokens or UI consistency.
A CSS-only spinner is a small build task; motion-quality mentions loading states but the ask is to build one, not judge motion.
CI pipeline setup is build automation, distinct from production observability, logging, or alerting.
A changelog is close to the release notes this skill explicitly covers, though the task is compilation more than prose craft.
A runtime version upgrade is a platform migration, outside package/dependency hygiene and this catalog's migration focus on data.
Greenfield dashboard design from scratch has no reference image, so image-to-ui does not apply and no design skill is listed.
